newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - Nov 5.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - Nov 5.

text.p: THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Australia's State and Territory Governments appear likely to reject the Howard Government's push to give the States increased responsibility for health, housing, education and child care at next week's Council of Australian Governments meeting in Brisbane amid concerns they would have to take on more responsibility for programs with less Commonwealth funding. Page 1.

The construction industry is preparing for increased costs following a deal in New South Wales, with major plumbing contractors receiving base wage rises of over 19 per cent during the next three years. The agreement follows a similar pay deal in Victoria which will deliver a 19.4 per cent pay increase over three years for site electricians. Page 3.

Today's Melbourne Cup has already delivered its first windfall - record turnovers for bookmakers and TABs around the country. Australian TABs are expected to take in over A$80.3 million from punters, with A$55 million expected to be invested in New South Wales TABS alone. Page 4.

Research conducted by academics from three universities has revealed that from amongst Federal election candidates, a surprisingly high proportion of Coalition respondents were more likely to be fearful of security threats from Asia and critical of Government assistance for Aborigines than their Labor counterparts. Page 5.
THE AUSTRALIAN

As the Reserve Bank faces increasing demands to ease monetary policy at its board meeting today on the back of evidence that economic activity has faltered, Federal Treasurer Peter Costello has set the scene for the central bank to cut official interest rates by highlighting low and falling inflation and wages pressures as "the matters on the mind of the Reserve Bank". Page 1.

The outspoken Independent member for the Queensland seat of Oxley, Pauline Hanson, yesterday questioned Prime Minister John Howard over whether Aborigines under the influence of alcohol, rather than her white supporters, had attacked visiting Singaporean defence personnel. Page 1.

In an unprecedented and vicious attack on the Criminal Justice Commission yesterday, Queensland Premier Rob Borbidge claimed the anti-corruption body was waging a "political vendetta" against State Police and Corrective Services Minister Russell Cooper ad treating him like "Queensland's most wanted man". Page 1.

Former New South Wales politician Frank Arkell has angrily rejected allegations he was a paedophile, claiming adults who abused the young should face the strongest penalties. Arkell said he was a victim of tall poppy syndrome, branding the New South WalesPolice Royal Commission, where he was called to give evidence, as a "Spanish inquisition". Page 3.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Following the release of the ANZ Bank jobs advertisements series, which fell for the fourth consecutive month signalling poor employment prospects for job seekers and confirming continued low inflation, economists said yesterday there is a strong case for the Reserve Bank to move to cut interest rates by 0.5 percentage points at today's board meeting. Page 1.

A new national Herald AGB-McNair poll, conducted at the weekend amid the continuing debate over race and immigration, has found Australians are deeply divided over the economic and social policy measures proposed by controversial Queensland
Independent MP Pauline Hanson. The survey found 62 per cent of respondents supported her call to freeze immigration. Page 1.

After Franca Arena named him in Parliament last week as Police Royal Commission witness W1 and after Royal Commissioner Justice Wood yesterday lifted his suppression order, former Lord Mayor of Wollongong and Independent New South Wales MP Frank Arkell says he is free to clear his name and sue his enemies. Arkell was named in Parliament two years ago as a pederast. Page 1.

A Herald investigation has found that, due to a crisis in permanent accommodation for people with severe intellectual disabilities, desperate parents are leaving their intellectually disabled children with temporary carers and refusing to take them home. The crisis has even driven some parents to attempt suicide. Page 1.
THE AGE

It has been revealed that Ken Baxter, a senior Victorian bureaucrat who oversaw massive job cuts to the State's public service, received over A$70,500 in director's fees from the Australian Dairy Corporation while he was still on the Victorian Government payroll, despite Commonwealth legislation requiring him to pay earnings from his work as corporation chair to the State Government. Page A1.

A Cambodian boy has testified in the ACT Magistrates Court that one of Australia's top diplomats, John Holloway, had sex with him in Phnom Penh in 1994 for US$2 on more than one occasion. Holloway, who is currently on leave from the Foreign Affairs and Trade Department, has not entered a plea for the hearing. Page A1.

As Melbourne Cup fever comes to head today, so too has the betting frenzy across the nation. The very enthusiastic Crown Casino chairman Lloyd Williams placed A$200,000 on local-hope Doriemus to win. Bookmakers yesterday reported a massive 33 per cent in re-cup betting from last year and solid interest from international punters for the race that will even see Federal Parliament suspended for a planned half-hour this afternoon. Page A1.

Federal Communications Minister Richard Alston is applying pressure on the national broadcaster, the ABC, to delay or even abandon its annual television coverage of the Sydney Gay and Lesbian Mardi Gras. Alston has asked ABC management whether community concern about the coverage should prompt a reassessment of the program. Page A1.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
